repos.description: Durable, file-based long-term memory for AI agents. Five-package plugin family: SDK, CLI, MCP server, Hermes adapter, and a LangGraph BaseStore. No vector database, no embeddings.

tweet.text:
Hermes 插件生态又燃爆了 🔥

Sibyl Labs 的零向量长期记忆、moonlight-lupin 的分门别类技能库、Adolanium 的额度倒计时面板、AtlasOmnia 的实战技能大礼包、Peteryhs 的实时天空皮肤……全网玩家把 Hermes 玩成了下一代「记忆宫殿 + 技能军火库 + 额度管家 + 生活工具箱 + 桌面美学大师」:

1️⃣ Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory（https://t.co/Phh99ontnd）

本地优先的 Agent 长期记忆：SQLite 存储、五层分级结构、全文检索，不用向量数据库也不用嵌入模型，自带 Hermes Agent 适配包，在 LongMemEval 公开评测里拿到 95.6%。
“不靠向量，也能记住你说过的每件事”！

2️⃣ moonlight-lupin/agent-skills（https://t.co/M7ZdwBD35S）

专为 Hermes Agent 写的技能合集，按领域分好类：https://t.co/sCmU1AI8VD 生图生视频、深度研究、人物背景调查、新闻定时摘要、NotebookLM 式资料库问答、多模型盲测对比……每个技能独立成文件夹，想装哪个装哪个。
“一个仓库，就是一整支专家团”！

3️⃣ Adolanium/hermes-resetwatch（https://t.co/29bNpa1nfH）

Hermes Desktop 插件：把 Nous、Claude、Codex、Cursor 等已登录账号的剩余额度做成实时进度条，再告诉你每个额度什么时候恢复；只用本机已有的登录，不爬供应商网站，5 分钟自动刷新。
“额度还剩多少、几点回血，一眼看穿”！

4️⃣ AtlasOmnia/hermes-custom-pack（https://t.co/UHeDdRArEY）

一套在真实 Hermes 环境里反复用过、改过的实战包：苹果提醒事项、应用安全审查、Obsidian 每日总结、新闻摘要脚本、旅行规划、Discord 接入、网页 QA 等技能和插件，每个都能单独安装，附带验证步骤。
“别人踩过的坑，直接变成你的技能”！

5️⃣ Peteryhs/zephyr（https://t.co/ADE53Lbe5v）

给 Hermes 桌面版换上更好看的界面：按你所在城市算日出日落、按实时天气变化的动态天空背景，面板跟着光线变色，还有浮动侧边栏、宽标签页和可以钉住的数据卡片；下载一个插件文件放进目录、重启就生效。
“连 Agent 的窗外，都有了真实的天空”！

repos.name: tradermonty/claude-trading-skills
repos.description: Claude Code skills for equity investors and traders — market analysis, technical charting, economic calendars, screeners, and trading strategy development.

tweet.text:
炒股时手一热就下单，亏了又想赶紧再炒一波低，结果仓位越做越重，事后连当初为什么买都说不清。

claude-trading-skills 是一位个人投资者开源的 Claude Code Skill 合集，把看大盘、算仓位、写交易日记、复盘这些事拆成了一个个 Skill。

我觉得最有意思的是下单前那道「纪律关卡」，没写交易计划、仓位超标、刚亏完想报复性加仓，都会被它拦下来，并记进交易日记。

GitHub：https://t.co/AA0kIfWaE8

日常用法也排好了，每天花 15 分钟过一遍市场状态，每周复盘一次持仓，每笔平仓都留记录，月底再回头看哪些规则该调。

基础流程不用订阅付费行情接口，拿公开的 CSV、K 线截图和本地文件就能跑。它不替人做买卖决定，管的是做决定的过程。

平时自己打理 ETF 和分红股，又总管不住手的，可以拿它给自己立几条规矩。

repos.name: googlecolab/google-colab-cli
repos.description: A CLI for interacting with Google Colab runtimes

tweet.text:
🚀 Google Colab 团队刚开源了 Colab CLI，在自己电脑的终端里一条命令就能借云端 GPU 跑脚本。

Colab CLI 上了 GitHub 热榜，GitHub 上已经 2400 多 star。

以前用 Colab，得打开浏览器、新建笔记本、把代码一段段贴进去、手动选 GPU，跑完再把结果一个个下载回来。

现在在本地终端里一条命令搞定：开一台新的云端机器，把本地脚本传上去跑、参数照转，跑完把输出文件取回来，再自动把机器销毁，不用惦记着关。

GPU 从 T4、L4 一直到 A100、H100 都能选，还有 TPU；想多折腾可以开交互式 REPL 或直接 SSH 进去，Google Drive 也能挂上。目前只支持 Linux 和 macOS，Windows 用户还得等等。

本地写代码、云端借 GPU，这下真的只隔一条命令了。

GitHub：https://t.co/oeW9flu10O

repos.name: shanselman/gputaskman
repos.description: A GPU task manager for Windows, Linux, and WSL: per-process VRAM, GPU activity, and LLM model/KV-cache insights for NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs (plus Huawei Ascend on Linux).

tweet.text:
🌡️ 本地跑模型必备的显存侦探 gputaskman，一眼看清你的显存到底被谁吃掉了。

gputaskman 出自微软的 Scott Hanselman，11 月 3 日才建仓，现在 3300 多 star，最近五天连发了 4 个版本。

本地跑大模型最抓狂的时刻：显存突然满了，任务管理器只告诉你某个进程占了一大块，至于是模型权重、KV cache 还是别的东西，完全看不出来。

gputaskman 是个终端里的 GPU 任务管理器，按进程列出显存和 GPU 活动，再把占用关联到已加载的运行时和模型文件，GGUF 模型还能拆出 LLM 缓冲区各占多少。Windows、Linux、WSL 和 Apple 芯片的 Mac 都能用。

作者自己也说得很坦白：还处在早期实验阶段，设备和进程计数器是实测值，模型那部分拆分是估算值，两者分开标。

显存焦虑，至少先知道它花在哪了。

GitHub：https://t.co/BUBG6kHkbw

repos.name: vas3k/TaxHacker

tweet.text:
Someone built a free, open source AI app that turns receipts and invoices into organized financial records automatically.

It’s called TaxHacker. Run it on your own server, upload a photo or PDF, and it can:

> Pull out items, prices, dates, merchants and taxes  
> Sort expenses and transactions into categories  
> Convert currencies using past rates, including crypto  
> Store records in a searchable database  
> Export reports for bookkeeping and tax prep

You can use a local AI model to keep your receipts and invoices on your own server.

TaxHacker is still in early development. It’s open source and free to self-host.

repos.name: ifixai-ai/iFixAi
repos.description: Independent Auditing of AI Agents. Run by human or the agent itself, to answer the most crucial question in the AI Agent Economy. Is the agent doing what is supposed to do? With iFixAi you can have this answer in less than 120 seconds.

tweet.text:
今天 GitHub 被「技能质检员 + Agent 剪辑师 + Agent 审计官 + 论文流水线 + 历史地图」联手屠榜了！

5 个星标暴增最狠的项目，专业拆解下！

1. NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator

英伟达出品的 Agent 技能「质检流水线」：先做不需要 API 密钥的确定性质量检查，再把装了技能和没装技能的两次运行放在一起对比，看这个技能到底有没有让 Agent 干得更好；pip 一装就能用，也能一行命令接进 CI，还能直接装给 Claude Code、Codex，问一句「我的技能好不好」。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/YwRvSXcdmk

技能满天飞的时代，终于有人出来当裁判了。953 星一天，总星 2,600+，英伟达亲自给技能发「质检合格证」！

🟢

2. kajisho5/ffmpeg-skill

给编程 Agent 配一个本地视频剪辑师：42 个基于 FFmpeg 的工具，剪辑、拼接、去静音、字幕卡拉 OK、横转竖、响度标准化、平台导出全都有；每个工具都能当 MCP 工具调用，剪完还会自己检查成片的时长、分辨率和画面，不上云、不要 API 密钥。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/dx765idmmo

一句话让 Agent 把长视频剪成 60 秒竖屏，还自带验片。475 星一天，总星 6,600+，剪辑师要开始紧张了！

🟢🟢

3. ifixai-ai/iFixAi

独立的 AI Agent 审计工具：把你的 Agent 放进一个模拟你业务的环境，发给它真实工作日会遇到的各种请求，包括诱它越权的请求，再由另一家模型来评分，找出它的错误和盲区；pip 一装，用内置演示 Agent 一分钟就能看到评分卡，Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 都能装插件直接说「审计我的 Agent」。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/Dr2iGB2ncd

Agent 上岗前先过一遍「入职背调」，越权的事当场抓包。313 星一天，总星 4.6 万+，Agent 合规赛道直接开卷！

🟢🟢🟢

4. google-research/paper-orchestra

Google Cloud AI Research 的多 Agent 论文写作框架：把想法和实验记录交给它，大纲、文献综述、分章写作、内容打磨、画图几个专职 Agent 接力干活，最后直接产出符合会议模板、可以投稿的 LaTeX 稿件。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/tCPmIURe76

从实验日志到投稿稿件，中间那段最熬人的路被 Agent 包了。306 星一天，Google 亲自下场写论文了！

🟢🟢🟢🟢

5. DeanChensj/jiangshan-map

江山时序：中国历史交互地图时间轴，从公元前 403 年一直拖到今天，18 个朝代、198 个疆域快照；点任意古城能看它两千多年的名称沿革和当地大事，搜一个历史人物能在地图上标出他一生的足迹，还能对照今天的省界。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/L7YafoQocS

读史书、背古诗再也不用脑补地图了，拖一下时间轴就是一部活的中国史。285 星一天，总星 6,600+，历史课代表狂喜！

🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢

⚠️⚠️
总结：
今天的榜单很清楚：技能和 Agent 已经多到需要「质检」和「审计」了。会造 Agent 只是入场券，能证明 Agent 靠谱，才是下一波真正的护城河。

repos.name: a2ui-project/a2ui
repos.description: Open-source generative UI framework: agents stream layout data, and apps render it with native components in React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.

tweet.text:
🧠 做 agent 应用的必备轮子 A2UI，让 AI 直接给用户生成能点能用的界面，而不是只回一段文字。

A2UI 上了 GitHub 热榜，已经 1.7 万 star、一千四百多个 fork，11 月 10 日前后刚把 Python SDK 和 CLI 一起发了新版。

以前做 agent 产品，想让 AI 返回一个表单或一张图表，要么让模型直接吐前端代码，安全和样式都管不住；要么自己写一堆解析逻辑兜底。

A2UI 换了个思路：界面用数据描述，不用代码。agent 只能从你预先定义好的组件目录里挑控件来拼，能做什么由 schema 卡死，再通过流式协议低延迟推到前端渲染。

前端这边 React、Angular、Lit、Flutter、SwiftUI 都有渲染器，agent 这边有 Python、TypeScript、Dart 的 SDK，还有接 MCP 的组件目录包。

以后 agent 回你的，可能不再是一段话，而是一个能直接点的界面。

GitHub：https://t.co/cerMPJjEXu

repos.name: liuhaisi2026212-maker/taishang-laojun
repos.description: 太上老君·AI炼丹炉：抖音/小红书短视频创作 Skill。不知道拍啥、不会写稿，丢给你的 AI：找对标拆爆款、选题、系列策划、口播稿、标题、复盘、去AI味。Claude Code / Codex 等 npx 一行安装，豆包等聊天智能体用 Bot 版。

tweet.text:
⚗️ 有点东西，太上老君·AI炼丹炉 能把抖音、小红书的短视频口播稿交给 AI 来写，不知道拍啥，它也能先帮你出选题。

太上老君·AI炼丹炉 是一个装进 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 就能用的技能，基于抖音创作者“柳爷不迷糊”的创作思路，豆包这类聊天智能体也有对应的 Bot 版。

做短视频最卡的通常是动笔：对着空白文档憋半天，写出来像说明书，发出去没人看完。

它把流程拆成七个模块：选材、看火、丹方、开炉、回炉、收丹、成丹，从找对标、拆爆款、做系列策划，到出口播稿、起标题、看后台数据复盘哪一段掉人，都有对应的一步。最新的 0.8.0 还加了“爆了一条之后，下一条怎么接”。

项目自己也说得实在：不承诺播放、涨粉或收入，经验来自对自己作品的口述复盘，不等于验证过的因果。

想做号又总卡在“拍什么、怎么说”，可以拿它先练起来。

GitHub：https://t.co/1SdxRcoSD7

itsmostafa 的 System One 万能连接器、mrnugget 的读心命令行补全、fazlerocks 的一分钟千封邮件分拣、jonathanavis96 的 Claude Code 全家桶、charlesdove977 的「Jev 分拣、Claude 动笔」技能……全网玩家把 Jev 玩成了下一代「决策插座 + 终端读心术 + 收件箱管家 + Agent 省钱包 + 分诊秘书」:

1️⃣ itsmostafa/system-one-connector（https://t.co/nNweCmHNHG）

把 Jev 直接接进 Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Codex、Hermes 和 Pi：Agent 问「这件事急不急」「该归哪个团队」，拿回一个概率或选项，代码里直接 if 判断；同一个连接器也能跑其他 System One 模型，包括自托管的 CLM、Laya；361 星。
“给每个 Agent 装一个快速决策插座”！

zsh 的 Fish 式自动补全，由 Jev 排序：你打字时，它拿最近 100 条不重复的历史命令问 Jev 你最可能在补哪一条，灰字显示在光标后并附上分数，按 → 接受；输入「last 5 commits」这种大白话，也能直接换成 git log --oneline -5；121 星。
“你刚开口，命令已经想好了”！

3️⃣ fazlerocks/jevmail（https://t.co/fjd4zu5kKx）

开源的 Gmail 邮件分拣：只读、本地运行，经 Vercel AI Gateway 调 Jev，把每封信分进「需要回复、通知、促销、销售、垃圾」五个托盘，再打 1~5 级紧急度；README 写着 1,000 封邮件约一分钟分完、花费约 3 美分；作者声明与 TypeSafe、Vercel、Google 无关；105 星。
“收件箱清零，只看需要你回的信”！

4️⃣ jonathanavis96/jev-kit（https://t.co/ZizpN3wAVA）

在 Claude Code 里用 Jev 的全套工具：给工具调用把关、给子 Agent 选合适档位，把 Jev 接进搜索、浏览、审查等环节；作者实测浏览器 Agent 改由 Jev 选每一次点击后，Claude 花费从每次 0.1868 美元降到 0.0008 美元，成功率同样 9/9；91 星。
“Jev 拍板，Claude 动笔，账单直接砍到零头”！

5️⃣ charlesdove977/claude-x-jev（https://t.co/ts0JZQS6Yx）

免费的 Claude Code 技能：一行 npx 安装，用一个 OpenRouter key 就能跑；/jev-classify 分拣任何东西，/jev-route 让 Jev 先分类、Claude 只读拿不准的，/jev-gate 在工具调用前加一道约 0.3 秒的安全检查；97 星。
“让 Claude 只读值得动脑的那部分”！

repos.name: alookai/alook
repos.description: Multi-Agent Collaboration for Team and Friends

tweet.text:
Always-on agents, clearly explained!

(and how to build one, 100% open-source)

An agent in a chat window only works while someone is typing to it. Once the tab closes, it stops and can't act on anything that happens next.

Always-on agents keep state across sessions and act without supervision. Anthropic's new guide on building them shows that the agent loop itself doesn't change, and everything new is the architecture around it.

The agent also isn't running all the time. It sleeps and wakes up for short runs, where each run receives an event, does the work, and saves what happened.

That cycle needs five primitives.

1) An event inbox

Webhooks, scheduled tasks, and user messages all land in a durable table instead of calling the agent directly. Direct calls let two events start competing runs, and a crash loses the event.

A single worker per inbox reads the table and starts runs. Events are deduplicated by source ID, and if a worker dies, a new one retries the pending event.

2) Timers

Follow-ups are deadlines the agent sets for itself, and schedules are recurring jobs. A scheduler polls for due timers and adds an event to the inbox, so every run still starts there.

3) Memory

Each run starts with a fresh context, so anything worth keeping lives in durable storage. The agent stores only what it can't look up again and keeps pointers for the rest.

Instructions, an index, and a log of what the user was already told load on every run. User notes and per-task progress files are read on demand, and anything that must survive compaction gets written during the run.

4) Permissions

This carries the most risk, since the run holds the user's access and nobody is watching. The agent sends requests without credentials, and a proxy adds them before forwarding.

For decisions that need a human, the agent makes a deferred tool call. The session is saved mid-call, the user sees an approval card, and the answer returns as an inbox event that resumes the session.

5) An outbox

The user gets the outcome, not every step. A run ends by sending a message, deciding nothing is worth sending, or asking for permission.

Too many messages make the agent noisy and too few miss what matters, so the guide recommends starting quiet and tuning it with evals.

Timers and user replies keep feeding new events into the inbox, and those short runs repeated indefinitely are what make the agent look always on.

I wrote a hands-on article that shows these ideas running in a real system built on Alook, an open-source, self-hosted platform that turns coding agents like Claude Code into an org chart with roles and real email inboxes.

Alook GitHub: https://t.co/vpAb0dy7AD

Anthropic's Guide on always-on agents: https://t.co/36fDMN5qsp

My article is quoted below. https://t.co/AZKpbT2Bvb

repos.name: ZiChuanLan/freebie-radar
repos.description: 白嫖与资讯资源聚合雷达：100+个源定时采集 + AI 二审过滤假福利 + 获取方式分级隔离抽奖/试用/推广 + Telegram 即时推送

tweet.text:
🛎️ 刷到一个白嫖党必装的自托管工具：资源雷达 freebie-radar，福利、好价、免费的开源项目，一有新的就推到你的 Telegram。

freebie-radar 上了 Trendshift 日榜，内置 63 个数据源，默认开 33 个，部署不需要外部数据库。

天天刷几个社区找羊毛，最累的是筛：一半是抽奖，一半是要拉人头的推广，真免费的反而被淹没。

freebie-radar 先用屏蔽词过一遍，再让 AI 二审，给每条标上类型、分类和获取方式：真免费、有条件、抽奖、试用、推广还是付费，一目了然，再打个 1 到 5 星。Telegram 推送可以开好几路，比如“只推真免费的软件”和“只推设了最高价的好价”分开发，晚上还能静音。AI 审核接任何 OpenAI 兼容接口，历史条目重新分类不花 Token。

羊毛得自己薅，筛选可以交给 freebie-radar。

GitHub：https://t.co/jceqo4wzmW

repos.name: Zagitta/gpu-unlock
repos.description: Your GeForce runs AI at half speed. This fixes it for 20/30/40 series cards. Up to 2× FP16 / BF16 / TF32 tensor throughput

tweet.text:
拿游戏显卡在本地出图、微调模型，总嫌速度不够快，第一反应往往是存钱换一张更贵的卡。

其实 RTX 20、30、40 系的游戏卡，在 AI 最常用的几种计算精度下，负责 AI 计算的张量核心只跑一半速度，同样的芯片做成专业卡就是全速。

gpu-unlock 这个开源项目就是把这道限速去掉，开机时赶在英伟达官方驱动接管显卡之前解锁，已斩获 19000+ Star。

GitHub：https://t.co/tZNQ83K1Rx

一张 RTX 3060 的矩阵算力从 27 涨到 51 TFLOPS，接近翻倍。换到实际任务上，ComfyUI 出图能快 30% 到 55%，LoRA 微调快 25% 到 50%。

不刷固件也不换驱动，解锁前后算出来的结果逐位一致，只是更快了。以后更新显卡驱动也不用重新弄一遍。

我觉得最划算的是一分钱不花，手上这张卡就能多出一截 AI 算力，本地经常跑 ComfyUI 的可以先拿它试试。

repos.name: BuilderIO/gpt-crawler
repos.description: Crawl a site to generate knowledge files to create your own custom GPT from a URL

tweet.text:
GitHub 上有个爬虫项目最近热度很高，专门给 GPT 用。

它干的事很直接：把指定网站的内容抓下来，整理成一个 Output.json 文件。

整个过程大概 30 秒，拿到文件后上传到 GPTS，一个基于该网站内容的问答机器人就能跑起来。

适合想把某个站点的资料变成自己专属助手的场景，不用手动一页页复制。

项目地址：https://t.co/SIO7dUUrwS

repos.name: Noniv/abyssal-garden
repos.description: A dreamy underwater world you can swim through in your browser: swaying kelp forests, sunbeams, a sunken ship and manta rays. Everything is generated by code with WebGPU (no images, models or sound files), all in a single 97 KB HTML file.

tweet.text:
🪸 浏览器里的海底乐园 Abyssal Garden 来了，打开网页就能潜进一片海底花园，海藻林、沉船、蝠鲼随便游。

Abyssal Garden 上了 Trendshift 日榜，整个世界装在一个不到 100KB 的 HTML 文件里，没有一张图片、一个模型、一段音频，全是代码现场生成的。

想放松一下，以前要么开个游戏等半天加载，要么看段海底视频，只能看不能动。

Abyssal Garden 双击就能游：WASD 移动，E 和 Q 上浮下潜，数字键一键跳到沉船、石头鲸尾这些景点。阳光从水面透下来，两百万片海藻在晃，耳边是实时合成的鲸鸣和气泡声，断网也能跑。电脑默认高画质，手机可以用低画质试试，不过触屏操作还是实验性的。

需要支持 WebGPU 的浏览器，比如桌面版 Chrome 或 Edge。

累了开一会儿，比刷短视频解压多了。

GitHub：https://t.co/YZCj6U5zsZ

repos.name: jlon/pi-harnessmm
repos.description: HarnessMM (arXiv 2610.32813) for pi: guarded decision reuse that runs a chain of dependent terminal steps inside one call instead of one model round trip per step

tweet.text:
Pi 扩展生态又燃爆了 🔥

repos.name: bryllim/workout-guide
repos.description: 302 open exercise illustrations and a framework-neutral npm package by Bryl Lim

tweet.text:
🏋️ 做健身 App 的素材神器 Workout Guide 来了，302 个健身动作插图全部开源，每个动作三帧，连起来就是动画。

Workout Guide 在 GitHub 已经 1.4K star，两百多个 fork。作者 Bryl Lim 在开源的 Everkinetic 姿势插图基础上补了动作和动画帧，又统一整理了资源和元数据。

自己做健身小程序或 App，最头疼的往往不是代码，是图：请人画太贵，网上找的风格不统一，还有版权问题。

现在装上 Workout Guide 的 npm 包，按动作名取图，或者按器械筛，比如只要徒手动作，一个函数调用就拿到。906 张透明背景的 SVG 不挑框架，还有一个能搜索的在线图库可以先挑着看。

授权也清楚：代码 MIT，插图 CC BY-SA 4.0，商用记得署名并按同协议共享。

健身 App 的插图预算，这下能省下来了。

GitHub：https://t.co/WZXAfSiNU2

majorminorlabs 的 Echo 音箱改造、nickvasilescu 的 AI 创作工作室、bruceleroyjr 的手表对讲机、tonbistudio 的投放看板、ateymoori 的口袋客户端……全网玩家把 Hermes 玩成了下一代「智能音箱大脑 + 影音工作室 + 腕上指挥官 + 营销仪表盘 + 随身 App」:

通过 Home Assistant 的 Assist，用一台刷了 echo-dot-assist 的旧亚马逊 Echo 跟你的 Hermes 对话；Echo Show 的屏幕还会同步显示它听到了什么、正在写的回答、正在用的工具，闲时显示后台任务；作者提醒买二手机前先核对型号和固件；706 星。
“旧 Alexa 换脑，客厅住进了 Hermes”！

2️⃣ nickvasilescu/parallax（https://t.co/ej16bKxY9s）

开源的 AI 图片、视频、音频工作室：画图、视频、配音、音乐各有工作台，还有社区、素材库、积分、开发者 API，以及能替你规划和制作的 Agent 聊天，可以跑在你自己的 Hermes 上；npm run dev 就能启动，没填模型 key 也能用示例文件全程体验；137 星。
“一个人，一整间 AI 影音工作室”！

在 Amazfit 手表上跟 Hermes 对话：点 TALK 说话，电脑用 Whisper 转写，答案先以文字出现在手腕上再读出来；Hermes 让 Claude Code 改文件时，手表弹出批准、拒绝、回复卡片，批准后可以关掉 App，结果发到 Telegram 再震你一下；26 星。
“抬手一点，就批准了一次代码修改”！

给 Hermes 桌面版加一个只读的营销页：广告花费对照总预算、投放节奏、剩余天数、从点击到转化的漏斗，按日投放、按版位/年龄/性别拆分、待你审批的方案和预算设置一目了然；它只读文件画图，从不改任何东西；17 星。

repos.name: steipete/summarize
repos.description: Point at any URL/YouTube/Podcast or file. Get the gist. CLI and Chrome Extension.

tweet.text:
两个小时的播客、四十分钟的 YouTube 视频，存下来的时候想着有空再看，结果一放就是好几个月。

summarize 这个开源工具，只需丢给它一个网页、视频、播客或者 PDF，它先把正文和字幕扒下来，再交给大模型写成摘要。

YouTube 和播客会先用现成的字幕和文字稿，没有才自己转写。视频还能按画面切出一张张幻灯片截图，带上时间点，翻起来很快。

GitHub：https://t.co/VJMELALxdW

不想敲命令的话，装个 Chrome 侧边栏插件就行，当前页面一键总结，看完还能接着跟页面内容聊。界面支持 14 种语言，简体中文也在里面。

模型这块很随意，自己的 API、本地 Ollama、OpenRouter 的免费模型都能接。已经登录好的 Codex、Claude 这类命令行工具也能直接拿来用，这点我觉得挺省心，不用另外再配一套。

稍后再看列表里堆了一堆长视频的，可以先拿它过一遍摘要，再决定哪些值得花时间看完。

repos.name: RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs
repos.description: Complete logs of the experiments in the blog post 'LLMs can understand and write neural network weights'

tweet.text:
🧐 颠覆认知，lm_understand-logs 公开了一组实验的全部过程：让大模型直接读懂、甚至从零写出神经网络的权重。

lm_understand-logs 上了 Trendshift 日榜，GitHub 已经 1.2K star，它是博文《Sparks of Weight Space Programming》背后八项实验的完整日志。

八个实验个个离谱：只看权重判断一个网络是拿哪个游戏训出来的、修好一个坏掉的网络、从零写一个 150 万权重的围棋网络、揪出一个爱拍马屁的语言模型、给模型提升数学能力。用的是 OpenAI 的 gpt-6-astra，通过 Codex CLI 调用。

很多 AI 研究只给结论，你没法知道模型到底是怎么做到的。这份日志把 1125 轮对话全摊开：发给模型什么、模型回了什么、跑了哪段代码、每个数值怎么评估，都在里面。Codex 自带的搜索、子代理这些工具全关了，每一轮都审计过是无工具轮次，想复核结论可以一轮一轮对着看。

AI 开始直接改 AI 的权重了，这份日志值得研究的人存一份。

GitHub：https://t.co/zJRNghXV48

repos.name: Eynnzerr/TelemetryCleaner
repos.description: 基于 Shizuku 免 Root 清除国产安卓 SystemHelper、RegService 等系统预装隐私数据收集模块

tweet.text:
🛡️ 细思极恐，国行安卓手机里预装的运营商组件可能一直在上报数据，TelemetryCleaner 能免 Root 把它们找出来卸掉。

TelemetryCleaner 上了 Trendshift 日榜，11 号建仓，几天里已经发到 v1.3。项目引用了 WiSec 2023 的流量测量：部分国行样机上能观察到运营商组件上报数据，小米和 ColorOS 样本里的中国移动组件上报了已安装软件列表。

以前想清掉这些系统预装组件，要么解锁 Root，要么自己敲 adb 命令，不少 ROM 还会在命令层直接拦住卸载。

TelemetryCleaner 借 Shizuku 拿到 shell 权限，Android 11 以上开个无线调试就能用：列出预装的运营商组件和它们的权限，按空间卸载并清掉数据，后悔了还能用系统保留的 APK 恢复。联通、OPPO、小米、华为的多个组件作者标了实测。

也要提醒一句：作者声明项目是学习用途，vivo 部分机型暂时只能冻结，还有人反馈卸掉 vivo 的 Device Management 后通话录音失效。动系统组件之前先想清楚，后果自己担。

手机里是谁在悄悄上报，自己心里得有数。

GitHub：https://t.co/8K78m4DpyI

repos.name: hridaya423/phonedriver
repos.description: MCP server and CLI that lets AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) see and control Android phones and iPhones. Reads the screen as text. Asks before it pays.

tweet.text:
想让 Claude Code 帮忙测一遍自己做的 App 应用，但无法帮忙操作手机点按钮、填表单、看界面，还得我们自己上手。

phonedriver 就是给 Agent 配了一台手机，Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这些都能直接操作安卓手机和 iPhone，模拟器和真机都行。

作者的演示挺直观，让 Claude Code 去点一份大号披萨，它自己找门店、加购物车、填结账信息，点到付款那一步停下来问人，最后没下单。

GitHub：https://t.co/6s9SoEsfMl

它把每一屏读成一张带编号的文字清单，模型按编号点，点完只回报界面上变了什么，不用每一步都截图。

作者拿 9 个手机任务做了对比，同样的活，mobile-mcp 用掉的 token 是它的 6.9 倍。

碰到付款先停下来问人，这点我觉得很关键，不然真不敢让它碰自己的手机。

做 App 的，让它把新用户第一次打开 App 的流程走一遍找 Bug，挺合适。

tweet.text:
This is f*cking insane.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei was asked what skills people should focus on as AI starts taking over more workplace tasks.

His message is becoming harder to ignore:

AI isn't just a productivity tool anymore.

It's learning to do the actual work.

Writing code, analyzing financial reports, building presentations, researching markets, handling customer support, and managing entire workflows.

And the scary part?

It's getting better every month.

Think about what this means for someone starting their career in 2026.

A company that once needed 5 junior employees might soon need just 1 person managing AI agents.

The question is no longer whether AI will change your career.

It's whether you'll know how to work with it.

If I were starting my career from scratch in 2026, I'd learn these 14 free resources:

1. Learn the foundations

→ Google AI Essentials: https://t.co/aCaRs4T3dc

→ Microsoft Generative AI for Beginners:
https://t.co/WKeWqNznw0

→ Elements of AI: https://t.co/pSYGpvMGK3

2. Master prompting

→ OpenAI Prompt Engineering Guide:
https://t.co/maqJL6BjMG

→ DAIR AI Prompt Engineering Guide:
https://t.co/bBqcLJyMwR

→ Anthropic Prompt Engineering Tutorial:
https://t.co/rTFQEgm3Sp

3. Learn to build AI agents

→ Hugging Face Agents Course:
https://t.co/XxVJXVsC1t

→ Microsoft AI Agents for Beginners:
https://t.co/dzuxf0wUtd

→ CrewAI: https://t.co/2KX6bJ3bEr

→ LangChain: https://t.co/XeuOPEjmzD

4. Understand how AI actually works

→ Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks Zero to Hero:
https://t.co/OuVgCfHcDV

→ Google's Machine Learning Crash Course:
https://t.co/uScGQznAX5

5. Build real-world projects

→ Awesome LLM Apps:
https://t.co/59h2VAtW0F

→ Anthropic Cookbook:
https://t.co/xnaZrtj5M5

Total cost: $0.

But here's what most people will get wrong:

They'll spend the next year collecting AI tools, watching tutorials, and saving resources.

Very few will actually build something.

Don't just learn how to prompt AI.

Learn how to:
• Break complex problems into smaller tasks.
• Build workflows that save hours.
• Connect different AI tools.
• Create and manage AI agents.
• Verify AI-generated results.
• Use AI to solve real business problems.

The future won't belong only to people who know how to use AI.

It will belong to people who know how to turn AI into results.

Don't spend 2026 watching the AI revolution happen. Learn how to build with it.

Save this and send it to someone starting their career.

tweet.text:
今天 GitHub 被「浏览器三巨头 + 安全扫描 + 代码审查」大厂联军屠榜了！

5 个星标暴增最狠的项目，专业拆解下！

1. GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src

Modern Web Guidance 的源码仓：把 Web 平台最佳实践和浏览器兼容数据做成技能，直接塞进你的编程 Agent，让它别再写过时套路；一行 npx 就能安装、搜索指南、扫描旧代码。由 Chrome、Edge、Firefox 和 MDN 团队共同维护。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/jfCyveI5ad

AI 写前端最大的毛病就是「十年前的 Stack Overflow 味」，这回浏览器厂商亲自下场补课。1,875 星一天，含金量拉满！

🟢

2. openai/codex-security

OpenAI 官方的 Codex Security 命令行和 TypeScript SDK：扫描仓库或 Git 改动、验证漏洞、生成补丁并复核修复，还能导出 SARIF/JSON/CSV，接 Linear、Jira、GitHub 和 CI。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/L47ZkoALHP

找漏洞、验漏洞、修漏洞一条龙，安全工程师多了个不下班的搭档。754 星一天，总星 1.3 万+，AppSec 正式进入 Agent 时代！

🟢🟢

3. tailscale/tailcat

Tailscale 官方的「不用 Tailscale 的 Tailscale」：像 netcat 一样在两台机器间开 WireGuard 端到端加密隧道，自动打洞直连，不需要账号、不需要 root，纯用户态命令行和 Go 库。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/IAzTAftQrk

一个短地址就能把两台机器连起来，穿透 NAT 像喝水一样简单。324 星一天，网络老炮狂喜！

🟢🟢🟢

4. alibaba/open-code-review

阿里内部用了两年的 AI 代码审查工具开源：读 Git diff，交给带工具调用的 Agent 去翻全文件、搜代码库，输出精确到行的结构化评审意见；README 称同模型下精确率和 F1 明显高于通用 Agent，token 只用约九分之一。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/52v05wxt3p

数万开发者、数百万缺陷练出来的审查官，现在人人能请。206 星一天，总星 5 万+，大厂内功直接外放！

🟢🟢🟢🟢

5. ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp

Chrome DevTools 官方给 Agent 的接口：MCP 服务 + 命令行，让 Claude、Cursor、Copilot 等编程 Agent 直接操控、检查一个真实 Chrome，录性能 trace、看网络请求、截图、读控制台。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/nyjMQvI3Vh

Agent 终于不再「盲写前端」，能自己打开 F12 找 bug 了。145 星一天，总星 5.5 万+，浏览器调试彻底交给 AI！

🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢

⚠️⚠️
总结：
今天的榜单写满了一个信号：大厂开始把自家内功直接喂给 Agent（Chrome 的 Web 指南和 DevTools、OpenAI 的安全扫描、阿里的代码审查）。工具越来越像「给 AI 用的」，谁先把 Agent 武装到牙齿，谁就站在下一波生产力的 C 位。

tweet.text:
Jev 应用分享又燃爆了 🔥

shitianfang 的 LLM + Jev 双人搭档、andududu 的 Jev 调用实况地图、tostechbr 的「话没说完就动手」语音控制、bytelabs-oss 的皇室战争机器人、AgriciDaniel 的技能分诊台……全网玩家把 Jev 玩成了下一代「快手搭档 + 调用监视器 + 读心语音助手 + 电竞选手 + 智能分诊员」:

1️⃣ shitianfang/jev-use（https://t.co/EQsfmfRyzt）

给 Claude Code、Codex 和 Pi 用的插件：不需要输出文字、只要快速判断的步骤交给 Jev，需要写内容时再交回大模型；作者实测拦截危险命令约 230 毫秒、不耗大模型 token，200 条消息 7 次调用完成上下文压缩；一行 npx 安装；72 星。
“写字交给大模型，拍板交给 Jev”！

2️⃣ andududu/jeview（https://t.co/NXaIU936hX）

一个非官方的本地 Jev 可视化网关：把 Jev 客户端指向它，它带着你的 key 转发请求，把每次调用存进本地 SQLite，并实时画在一张地图上；只需 Node 24，零依赖；作者声明与 TypeSafe 无关联；68 星。
“每一次 Jev 判断，都看得见”！

3️⃣ tostechbr/partway（https://t.co/wONjCwwhGk）

macOS 语音控制：你说的每个词都拿去问 Jev，约 200 毫秒返回带概率的判断，所以一句话还没说完，备忘录就已经打开了；能开应用、新建笔记、开网站、搜索、打字，还能一口气连说多个指令；32 星。
“你还在说，它已经做完了”！

repos.name: patchy631/time-to-first-token
repos.description: A 10-week, 30-minutes-a-day roadmap for LLM inference serving and optimization. vLLM, SGLang, quantization, speculative decoding, benchmarking.

tweet.text:
GPU architecture, clearly explained.

The usual assumption is that a faster GPU means more compute, so a chip rated for more operations per second should generate more tokens per second.

That rarely holds. You can rent a top-end chip, load a model, watch utilization sit high, and still get a few dozen tokens per second out of hardware capable of a thousand trillion operations.

The arithmetic units are not the limit. They spend most of their time waiting for numbers to arrive.

Memory bandwidth is how fast those numbers can be delivered, and it grows far more slowly than arithmetic capability with each new generation.

The H100 makes this concrete. It does 989 trillion operations per second at 16-bit precision, while its memory delivers 3.35 trillion bytes per second.

Divide one by the other and you get about 295. That is how many operations the chip has to perform on every byte it fetches just to keep its arithmetic units busy.

Generating a token comes nowhere close. Each weight gets multiplied by one number and added into a running total, so two operations per weight, and each weight costs 2 bytes to read at 16-bit precision.

That works out to 1 operation per byte, roughly three hundred times short of what the chip needs.

Once you see that, the layout of a GPU stops looking arbitrary. All of it is organized around distance, because every trip to fetch a value is the expensive part.

Execution is nested in four steps, smallest first.

→ Thread. The smallest unit of work, doing arithmetic on its own handful of values.

→ Warp. A group of 32 threads that move in lockstep and share a single instruction, which is what the hardware actually schedules.

→ Thread block. A batch of warps, up to 32 of them or 1024 threads, handed to one compute unit and staying there until it finishes.

→ SM. The streaming multiprocessor, a small self-contained machine with its own arithmetic units, its own storage, and its own scheduler. An H100 has up to 132 of them.

Memory is nested along the same lines, and that is the part that decides your speed.

→ Registers. 256 KB per SM, split so each thread gets a private slice nobody else can read. A value here already sits next to the thing that needs it, so reading it costs nothing worth measuring.

→ Shared memory and L1. A few hundred KB per SM. Shared memory is the only level you place things into yourself, and every thread in a block can read it, which is where the name comes from.

→ L2 cache. Around 50 MB sitting below all the SMs, and the first level every one of them can see. Reaching it means leaving your own SM.

→ HBM (High Bandwidth Memory). Around 80 GB, holding model weights, the KV cache, and activations. It sits outside the processing chip entirely, and reaching it is the slowest thing a GPU does.

The nesting is what buys you speed. Anything that stays inside one SM is fast because nobody outside needs to see it, and anything the whole chip has to agree on pays for the trip down.

Add up the registers across every SM and you get roughly as much storage as the L2 underneath them, which is nothing like the neat pyramid you see on a CPU.

So making a GPU faster is mostly about how many round trips to HBM you can avoid. FlashAttention is the clearest case, since ordinary attention writes a large intermediate result all the way down and reads it back, while the tiled version keeps it up on the SM and runs far faster doing the same arithmetic.

I wrote the full breakdown of how a GPU works, from this layout up to the ratio that sets your token rate. The article is quoted below.

I have also put together a 10-week, 30-minutes-a-day roadmap for engineers who want to actually run LLM inference in production, not just read about it.

Check this out: https://t.co/pOqkWvDJ2d

(don't forget to star 🌟)

Stay tuned for more on this! https://t.co/LZBmYCeFnK

repos.name: bookleme/bookleme
repos.description: 读了么（BookLeme）· 把一本书编译成 Agent Skill —— 双引擎 + 可插拔体裁插件 + 逐字忠实度回验

tweet.text:
📗 脑洞大开，BookLeme（读了么）能把一整本书编译成 AI agent 可以直接安装的 Skill，让 agent 带着这本书的方法干活。

BookLeme 刚开源没多久，核心只用 Python 标准库，PDF、EPUB、DOCX、MOBI 等七种格式都能吃。

以前想让 AI 按某本书的思路做事，只能把书整本扔进对话里，上下文塞不下，回答还经常跑到书外去。

BookLeme 让书走一遍 S0 到 S9 的十段流水线，产出两种东西：一种是查资料用的知识包，一种是能改变 agent 做事方式的 Skill，比如按书里的方法陪你做教练式对话。

它还把「忠实度」拆成 7 个可以量化的指标，README 里写一本 273 页的中文书跑下来，覆盖率是 1.00。

版权这块也做得很克制：单条引文不超过 150 字，总引文比例不超过 3%，用别人的书生成的 Skill 默认私有，想公开分发得额外加两道确认参数。

读完一本书不难，难的是让 AI 也照着它做事。

GitHub：https://t.co/p66N7QtIp2

repos.name: MarcosSete/awesome-free-ai-books
repos.description: A curated list of free, legitimate AI/ML books

tweet.text:
📕 想系统学 AI 的，先收下这份免费书单 Awesome Free AI Books，深度学习、强化学习到大模型的经典教材全是官方免费版。

Awesome Free AI Books 只收作者或出版社官方免费放出的书，链接都指向作者主页、大学或开放许可出版方，Scribd、Z-Library 这类来源一律不收。

以前想找一本经典教材的电子版，搜出来一半是来路不明的网盘，下到的还可能是缺页的旧版。

这份清单按方向分好了类：深度学习有 Goodfellow 等人那本《Deep Learning》和 2023 年的《Understanding Deep Learning》，强化学习有 Sutton 和 Barto 的第二版，概率机器学习有 Kevin Murphy 的两卷本，往后还有统计学习、计算机视觉、因果推断、图神经网络和 AI 安全。

仓库本身不托管任何文件，只做目录，用 CC0 协议开放。

正版教材就免费放在那，缺的只是一份靠谱的目录。

GitHub：https://t.co/GRoHlzFExU

repos.name: openfilm/openfilm
repos.description: The open source AI video agent: turns any coding agent into a video agent, with editors to change anything it makes.

tweet.text:
用 HTML 和 CSS 做视频，这个思路我第一眼觉得有点怪，看完演示又觉得挺合理，毕竟 Agent 最熟的就是写网页。

OpenFilm 是一个开源的 AI 视频 Agent，让 Codex、Claude Code 这类编码 Agent 来做视频，片子里的每个镜头其实都是一个网页。

跟它说一句「给我的命令行工具做一条 20 秒的发布视频，配上音乐」，它就开始写，本地的编辑器会在浏览器里显示片子一点点成形。

GitHub：https://t.co/z8ZgeFDsaA

做完不满意，每个元素都还能改。文字、颜色、位置可以直接动手调，时间线上能裁剪片段，也可以继续让 Agent 改。

自带一个免费素材库，音乐、音效、配音、贴纸、转场和模板都有。做片、剪辑、导出都不需要账号，还能导出给 Final Cut Pro、Premiere 和达芬奇接着剪。

支持 macOS、Windows、Linux 系统，另外有 macOS 和 Windows 的桌面版，装好就能用。官方那条 1 分 42 秒的发布视频，就是用它从头做到尾的。

repos.name: swipt-automation/swipt
repos.description: The universal iOS automation platform

tweet.text:
👆 iPhone 自动化的新外挂 Swipt，让 AI agent 直接上手操作你的 iPhone 和 iPad。

Swipt 刚开源没多久，对 iOS 27 做了第一梯队支持，iOS 17.4 到 26 也在支持范围内，不过作者说手头没有这些版本的设备，没实测过。

以前想自动化点手机，要么自己从头写测试脚本，要么靠按坐标点击的录制工具，界面一变就失灵。

Swipt 底层基于 CoreDevice 和辅助功能服务，对外提供兼容 MCP 的接口：支持 MCP 的 agent 接上之后，就能在一个 JS 环境里直接控制 iPhone 或 iPad，顺带管理和调试 Swiplet；想要更全的能力，还有配套的命令行工具。

Swiplet 是用 SwiftUI 写、直接跑在 Swipt 里的小应用，自动化流程也能做成一个个独立的小程序。

手机以前要用手指点，现在可以交给 agent 点了。

GitHub：https://t.co/HwMGaxvdc9

repos.name: agentes-chat/agentes-chat
repos.description: Open-source, self-hosted Slack alternative where your team and AI agents work together in channels and DMs. Agents run on Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini or Grok, with MCP tools, their own computer and browser, routines, memory and approvals. Web, desktop and phone apps. Docker Compose + Postgres. AGPL-3.0.

tweet.text:
团队里用上了 Agent，可它们各待在各的窗口里，谁让它干了什么、干到哪一步，别的同事基本看不到，交接全靠截图转述。

https://t.co/pFzUO9u0EA 是一个开源、可以自己部署的团队聊天工具，定位是 Slack 的替代品，特别的地方是 Agent 和人待在同一个频道里。

每个 Agent 有自己的角色、负责人和每月预算，在频道里看得到对话，轮到它时才接话，干活过程所有人都能看见。

GitHub：https://t.co/KG03DriUKG

合并代码、上线部署这类敏感操作，会在聊天里弹出一张卡片，等负责人点了批准才执行。每次调用模型的花费也都记在对应 Agent 名下。

让 Agent 动手前先问一句，这个设计我觉得挺实在。

Agent 还有自己的电脑和浏览器。浏览器功能还在测试，操作时能在聊天里实时看着，碰到登录或验证码可以接手，弄完再交还。

模型可以接 Claude、OpenAI、Gemini、DeepSeek、Kimi 等，一条命令装到 Linux 服务器上，官方说大约 10 分钟就能跑起来。

repos.name: saragordic/window-sweaters
repos.description: A macOS menu-bar app that dresses your windows in knitted borders.

tweet.text:
🧶 太可爱了，Window Sweaters 能给你 Mac 上的每个窗口都织一件毛衣。

Window Sweaters 在 GitHub 已经 1400 多 star，也上了 HelloGitHub 的推荐。

Mac 桌面一开一堆窗口，边框都是一个样，哪个是哪个全靠认。

装上它之后，每个窗口外面多了一圈针织边框，而且按应用配色：作者给 37 个常用应用手工挑了专属毛衣，覆盖 Apple 自带应用、办公、编程与 AI、设计工具和 Office 全家桶；其他应用会从图标里取色，自动织出锯齿、野餐格或闪烁图案。

菜单栏里能调花样、边框宽度和针脚大小，不想给某个应用穿毛衣，取消勾选就行。

提醒一句：它还没过 Apple 公证，第一次打开可能被系统拦下；它用的是 macOS 私有窗口 API，系统一更新可能就得等作者适配。项目基于 JankyBorders 做的，GPL-3.0 开源。

天冷了，给窗口也添件衣服。

GitHub：https://t.co/qN6i36y1yj

repos.name: cloudflare/kitesurf
repos.description: Kitesurf is an experimental browser engine that runs on Cloudflare Workers.

tweet.text:
🪁 Cloudflare 刚开源了 Kitesurf，让 agent 不用开 Chrome 也能打开网页、跑 JS、截图。

Kitesurf 是 Cloudflare 官方出品的实验项目，已经上了 Trendshift 日榜。

以前想让 agent 自动浏览网页，基本得起一个无头 Chrome 或者浏览器容器，又吃资源又难扩容。

Kitesurf 直接把浏览器引擎搬进了 Cloudflare Workers：解析 HTML、套 CSS、执行页面里的 JavaScript、渲染截图都在 Worker 里完成，每个页面跑在单独隔离的 worker 里。它支持 Chrome DevTools 协议，Puppeteer 这类客户端可以直接连上来用。

引擎底下拼的是一串开源 Rust 项目：Stylo 管 CSS，Boa 在 WebAssembly 里跑 JS，Krilla 还能顺手输出 PDF。

要说清楚的是：Kitesurf 目前还是实验性项目，要用到 Workers 付费计划里的 Dynamic Workers，自身也不带认证，部署后得自己在前面加一层访问控制。

给 agent 用的浏览器，正在从容器里搬到边缘节点上。

GitHub：https://t.co/8iyHGMznRJ

repos.name: Liuzedooong/SparseReading
repos.description: Saving your tokens 🔥! SparseRead enables AI agents to selectively read what matters across diverse information sources.

tweet.text:
Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences cut AI-agent token consumption by up to 92.9%, without retraining a single model.

They also reduced execution time by up to 89%.

The problem is familiar if you've built AI agents. Ask a coding agent to investigate one error, and it may read an entire log, repository file, or document when only a few passages are relevant.

Those unnecessary tokens can remain in context across subsequent model calls, increasing cost and latency.

The researchers developed SparseRead, a system that controls what an agent reads before the content enters the model's context.

It works through three components →

1./ Read Intent Protocol: Tracks what information the agent needs, which evidence has been found, and what remains unresolved.

2./ Adaptive Reader Backends: Locate relevant evidence across documents, PDFs, code repositories, and structured data.

3./ Budgeted Read Gate: Limits how much source content enters context, with the option to fall back to reading the complete file.

Across six models and five workload scenarios, the researchers reported →
> Up to 92.9% fewer tokens consumed.
> Up to 89% less execution time.
> Median reductions of 61.4% in tokens and 53.7% in time.
> Task quality preserved or improved in most evaluated settings.

No model retraining is required.

The interesting engineering lesson is that context optimization doesn't have to begin with compression or KV caching.

You can reduce a substantial amount of work by controlling what enters the context in the first place.

(Link to the paper and code in comments)

repos.name: delef/ClamDown
repos.description: Keep coding agents working on a MacBook with the lid closed. Free menu bar app: no sleep, fan control by CPU temperature, screen lock, battery and heat cut-offs.

tweet.text:
让 Claude Code 跑一个长任务，人又要出门，MacBook 只能半开着盖子拎在手上，一合上任务就停了。

ClamDown 是一个 Mac 菜单栏小工具，打开开关后合上盖子也不睡眠，Agent、终端和下载都接着跑。

合盖时系统会把风扇压在低速，它会按 CPU 温度调风扇，默认 60 度以下最低速，到 85 度满速。合上的同时还会锁屏。

GitHub：https://t.co/RdnT316saZ

电量掉到 10%、机器过热或者定时结束，它会自己关掉开关让 Mac 正常睡眠，并发通知说明原因。

就算应用崩溃或退出，后台的辅助程序约 90 秒收不到心跳，也会把睡眠、低电量模式和风扇恢复原样。

免费开源，安装包经过苹果公证，macOS 13 及以上能用。合盖以后温度和电量都有人盯着，背着出门跑任务也放心多了。

repos.description: 3,516 curated Figure 1 / teasers from ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS, CVPR, ACL, AAAI (2023-2026), with tier badges and FigureForge retrieval-augmented figure drafting

tweet.text:
论文写完了，放在开头讲清整个方法的那张主图还空着，框框箭头摆了半天，看着总像组会汇报的 PPT，不像顶会论文里的图。

「顶会论文主图灵感画廊」收录了 ICLR、ICML、NeurIPS、CVPR、ACL、AAAI 在 2023 到 2026 年的 3452 张论文主图。

能按会议、年份、录取等级和图的类型筛选，也能按标题、作者、关键词搜。Oral、Spotlight 和获奖论文的图还带角标。

GitHub：https://t.co/MznDqmo9UH

自带的 FigureForge 能帮忙出初稿，贴上标题和摘要或者上传 PDF，勾几张同类参考图，它先归纳版式和配色再生成。

可以导出 SVG，拿到 Figma、https://t.co/tqzUUaWAeq 里接着改。整个过程在浏览器本地跑，模型密钥要自己准备，只存在本机。

纯静态网页，克隆下来双击就能打开，也有在线版。每张图都链接原论文，画图前翻一翻，比自己硬想省事多了。

repos.name: bryanyzhu/agentic-ai-system-course
repos.description: Use agent to learn agent - A skeleton course on how to design, build, and operate production AI agents

tweet.text:
🏫 想把 AI agent 真正做上线的看这里，Agentic System Course 用 22 章讲透生产级 agent 怎么设计、搭建和运维。

Agentic System Course 的 fork 已经接近一百个，而且整套课是写给你和你的 AI 一起读的，仓库里同时放了 AGENTS.md 和 CLAUDE.md。

以前学 agent 开发，要么跟着某个框架的教程一步步敲，换个技术栈就全废；要么零散看博客，记忆、多 agent 协作、成本控制各讲各的。

这门课只给骨架：把记忆与状态、多 agent 协调、外部接口、可观测性、成本与延迟、安全运维这些承重的主题和取舍讲清楚，具体代码交给你的 AI 按你的技术栈去补。最后一章是一张设计画布，直接拿来设计你自己的 agent。

还有个顺手的：仓库自带一个评审 skill，把你的 PRD、设计文档或 agent 代码丢给它，它先判断你做的是个人项目、团队工具还是面向客户的产品，再挑相关章节出报告，每条问题都带严重程度、证据、章节出处和修复建议。课程拿 OpenCode、Hermes Agent、OpenClaw、Paperclip 四个开源项目当参考实现。

用 agent 学 agent，这个思路挺对味。

GitHub：https://t.co/9mBRsegE03

repos.name: Innei/ryugi
repos.description: Ryugi (ryoo-ghee) — Interactive Artifacts for Coding Agents: artboards of mockups, design docs, whiteboards, HTML benches and verify reports you comment on, with every comment sent back to the agent.

tweet.text:
✨ 眼前一亮，Ryugi 让 Claude Code 这类编码 agent 把方案直接画在页面上给你看，你在哪里点、评了什么，反馈都原路回到那个会话。

Ryugi 的作者是 Innei，GitHub 主页写着在做 LobeHub；项目从 Superpowers v7.0.0 分出来，11 月 12 日一天就连发了四个版本。

以前让 agent 出个界面方案或设计思路，它只能在终端里用文字描述，你脑补半天，回一句「左边再窄一点」，它又重写一大段。

Ryugi 给了五种页面：画板、文档、白板、HTML 和验证页。agent 把方案画出来，你直接在页面上选中、评论，点通过或驳回，裁决回到创建页面的那个 agent 会话。东西都存在你自己的项目里，由本地服务器打开，要分享再生成链接。

验证页也挺实在：agent 说「做完了」时，会逐条列出它跑了什么来核实、附上原始输出，没验证的也单独列出来并写明原因。

Ryugi 会替换 Claude 自带的托管 Artifacts，Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 等也能用。要留意它现在用的是自定义的源码可见许可，不是开源许可。

让 agent 少说多画，你也少猜一点。

GitHub：https://t.co/NQSAGMYUR7

repos.name: JDhruv14/line-art-animation
repos.description: A Claude skill and TypeScript library for animated line-art SVG components: ink figures that walk and react, scenes with a day/night cycle.

tweet.text:
想给个人网站加点有意思的插画动画，找来的素材不是太花，就是一放大就糊，动起来还有点僵。

line-art-animation 是一个 Claude Skill 加一套 TypeScript 小库，专门做线稿风格的动画组件，墨线画的小人会走路、骑车，被点一下还有反应。

全部用 SVG 实时绘制，放多大都清晰，也会跟着鼠标互动。场景能从白天过渡到夜晚，天黑以后窗户和灯笼会亮起来。

GitHub：https://t.co/mBIXlIKbuf

仓库里带了一个日式小街的完整示例，有茶馆、澡堂、运河、猫和船夫，十来处都能点，拖动太阳就能改时间。

让 Claude 做的时候，它会先画一个人物给我们确认，再搭剩下的部分，交付前逐帧检查动作。还能照着参考视频复刻走路姿势，导出成视频。

腿的动作是算出来的，落地那只脚会稳稳踩住、不打滑，这个细节我挺喜欢。库里 4 个模块都没有外部依赖。

repos.name: Omodaka9375/browserr
repos.description: Servo-based headless browser engine for AI agents. An auditable alternative to embedding Chromium.

tweet.text:
给 Agent 用的浏览器，不用再套 Chromium 了

Browserr 刚开源，是个跑在 Servo 上的无头浏览器引擎，专门给 AI 智能体用的

它不走 CDP 那套上千个接口，整个协议就 22 条命令，JSON 走本地回环，一个下午能审计完

MCP 是原生的，直接给 42 个工具，Claude、Codex 这些能接 MCP 的客户端不用写集成代码就能用

一个二进制文件大概 120MB，零依赖，默认 CPU 渲染，没显卡的机器、容器、树莓派都能跑

设计上是 fail-closed，不确定的请求先拦下来，5 秒没人拍板就拒绝，付钱和验证码必须人来确认

验证码、一次性码、付款页面能自动识别，pause 一下把页面交还给真人，截图上每个元素都编了号，人和智能体指着同一个东西说话

每次操作都留证据，带时间戳的截图加一份只追加的操作日志

React 18 和 Vue 3 都能跑，Windows、Linux、macOS 都有包，Python 3.10 以上就能用

刚开源 4 天，仓库在 Omodaka9375/browserr，Apache-2.0 协议

Official skills from the Expo team that help Claude Code build, debug, upgrade, and deploy iOS and Android apps.

Get PostgreSQL, GraphQL APIs, authentication, storage, and functions in one backend stack. Includes an MCP server for AI coding assistants.

Skip the blank project. Start your SaaS with authentication, database setup, Stripe integration, email tools, and reusable UI components.

Add a drag-and-drop page editor to your React app. Use your own components and let users customize pages visually.

https://t.co/YPwnTn6M0M

Build an AI chat interface with streaming responses, attachments, Markdown, retries, and conversation components already handled.

https://t.co/aGSEGj92EP

A mobile app foundation with Expo, navigation, TypeScript, UI components, and separate development, staging, and production configurations.

https://t.co/0jXNksqDbT

Give Claude Code customizable, shadcn-style mobile components. Build polished screens without recreating every button, dialog, and input.

https://t.co/JfLcoCULFa

Turn your app into a paid product. Add subscriptions, track usage such as tokens or API calls, and generate invoices.

repos.name: oil-oil/agy-fast-io
repos.description: 让 Antigravity 少走回合、少等审查的本地规则插件（非官方）

tweet.text:
最近非常高强度地使用了 Antigravity 和 Gemini 模型，说说自己的感受和一些实用技巧：

1. 在 Gemini 4 Carbon 出来之前，我一直用的是 Gemini 4 Argon。200 刀套餐的额度很多，在我重度开发、适当搭配 Codex 进行 review 的情况下，周额度到最后一两天还得单独搞点重活才能用得完，所以大多数情况下可以爽用。现在 Gemini 4 Carbon 出来之后，任务效果比 Argon 更好，并且消耗并没有高多少，几乎和之前使用 Argon 是一样的。

但是即便是 Gemini 4 Carbon，我自己的感受也是不如 使用 Claude Opus 5.5 的。Claude 给人的感觉是心思更加缜密，更加让人安心。比如在一个复杂仓库里面，一些分支管理、版本管理这些都是 Claude 会更稳定，而且它会主动告诉你当前存在什么问题，审美和开发能力也还是 Claude 更强。

Gemini 的优势在于订阅门槛很低，而且比起 Codex 来说，交流感好太多了，文案能力也强。如果平时需要让 AI 辅助写写课程、做做视频脚本，那么 Gemini 是目前唯一的选择。

2. Gemini 4 不同的型号都是比较自信的模型，所以它给的方案以及它写的代码，经常缺胳膊少腿，它自己就觉得很不错，结果给其他模型看完了发现一大堆问题。

而且虽然说话有人味儿，但是会过度浮夸，喜欢加很多拟人、形容、比喻，给你很多情绪价值。如果用来开发复杂项目，一定要搭配其他的模型来帮助它 review，比如说另一个极端的 GPT。我自己一直都是用 GPT 来帮助 Gemini 评审方案和代码的，搭配起来使用效果非常好。

3. Antigravity 的 harness 很垃圾，读文件速度巨慢。而且如果我们开的是 Turbo 模式，虽然很多工具调用不会征求我们人的同意，但它一定会走一下云端审核，甚至很多读文件的命令都需要审核。

这个云端审核每一次大概 1 到 3 秒，你在执行一个复杂任务的时候，有可能审核好几十次，就会浪费好几分钟的时间用于这个云端审核。而且 Antigravity 读文件也不够高效，每一次读完文件都得思考，然后再去读下一个文件；单个文件读了几行，它还得思考完再读后面的几行；还有就是每一次任务完成的回答都是非常长的。

为了解决这个问题，我自己写了一个 Antigravity 的插件，整理了不需要走审核的白名单命令，并且提供了一些提示词，告诉 Antigravity 怎么样去高效地读代码：https://t.co/qSaMQ5yXWo

4. Gemini 4 Hydrogen 发布之后，也能够一定程度解决 Antigravity 读文件速度慢的问题。Antigravity 原生的子 Agent 仅支持 inherit / flash_lite / flash / pro 四个档位，这里竟然没有 Gemini 4 系列的模型。

但是 Antigravity 内部有一个叫做 swarm 的 Skill，相当于一个多 Agent 协作系统，这个 Skill 支持派发任何模型的子 Agent，甚至可以派发 Antigravity 里面的 Claude 模型。我的做法是通过我自己开发的另一个 Skill 套件 oil-dev-skills（https://t.co/PpWpMIgIcp），里面有一个 oil-explore，我们把 Antigravity 需要使用 swarm + Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Low) 探索代码作为规则配进去，后续在新的项目里面新开话题的时候，探索代码的速度就会非常快。

5. Antigravity 里面还有一个 Orchestrator 模式（比如 Orchestrator Carbon），它的机制其实就是计划模式，先用能力强的模型去探索代码、写方案，然后再让比较便宜的模型，比如说 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 去基于方案执行，但是现阶段对我来说，我觉得 Carbon 写代码尚有提升空间，更何况 Hydrogen 了，所以我会先在一些简单的项目里面测一下，现在测试得还不够多，所以不给大家结论

这个模式对单纯读文件、问问题其实没有加速帮助，因为读代码全在第一阶段，跑的还是最慢的规划模型，平时只看代码直接选 swarm + Hydrogen 反而更快。

tweet.text:
An open-source, self-hostable layer that turns your agents into a team working toward shared goals.

It's called Rowboat, and it can bring Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes into one team. Any agent that supports MCP can join too, so you stop being the glue between your AI agents.

You send one message, and a super agent:

- Decides which agents the job needs

↳ Runs on the subscriptions or API keys you already have
↳ See every handoff, and step in whenever you want
↳ Or let Rowboat host your agents, if you'd rather not run servers
↳ Free to use

I loaded nine weeks of product data for a sample app into PostHog, a product analytics tool, and asked the super agent why new users weren't coming back. Hermes found where they dropped off in PostHog, Claude Code found why in the user feedback, and Codex built the dashboard.

repos.name: ModernRelay/omnigraph
repos.description: Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology

tweet.text:
I have been building with coding agents for over 2 years now.

Here's the one mistake I see devs make when they run several agents in parallel:

They give each agent its own branch of the code, but let every agent write straight into the same shared data.

Say Claude Code and Codex both pick up a task on the same record, and both read it at the same moment.

Codex finishes first and saves its change.

Claude Code is still working from the copy it read at the start, which is now out of date. When it saves, it writes that old copy back and erases Codex's change.

Neither agent gets an error, and the next agent that queries the data never sees what Codex did.

Code doesn't have this problem, because every change goes on a branch and gets checked at merge, but agents operating on data don't have a parallel stack.

Finally, devs have open-sourced a graph database with the Git model built in.

Omnigraph is an open-source graph database that versions your agents' data the way Git versions code. Each agent writes on its own branch, and every merge is checked against the latest main before it lands.

Here's the repo: https://t.co/7wZg7yh0H3

(don't forget to star it 🌟)

The image below compares it with a standard graph DB:

Standard graph DB
- Every agent writes in place on one live graph
- The last write wins, even when it came from an out-of-date copy
- The next query reads mixed context, so the final answer rests on a stale change

Omnigraph
- A policy gate blocks direct writes to main
- Each agent writes on its own branch, isolated until it merges
- A merge check sees that Claude Code started from an old version, flags the conflict, and Claude Code retries from the latest main
- Every merge becomes a commit you can diff or roll back

It's written in Rust, and agents connect to it over MCP, a TypeScript SDK, or the CLI.

If you want to dive deeper, Avi wrote a full breakdown of why shared agent data needs branches, diffs, and merge checks, not just row locks.

It walks through a real run with two Claude Code agents, from the refused merge to the clean retry. Read it below.

Read it below. https://t.co/Qks4NHoghv

tweet.text:
GitHub is hiding some SCARY GOOD tools for X creators.

I found 10 free repos that can help you hunt viral ideas, create better posts, and automate hours of work.

This feels unfair:

1. Twitter Web Exporter

Turn your X bookmarks into an idea bank. Export the posts and lists you load in your browser as CSV, JSON, or HTML so you can search and sort them later.

https://t.co/ts4hkSTLrV

2. twscrape

Stop scrolling your feed for ideas. Search X from Python or the terminal and collect posts on topics you cover. It requires a logged-in account and uses unofficial endpoints.

https://t.co/EUw9wWbt8z

3. Cheat on Content

Score your draft before you publish. Three days later, compare your prediction with the real numbers and use what you learn to judge the next draft.

https://t.co/cuE7tgBfSM

4. PRAW

Pull rising posts and discussions from the subreddits your audience reads. Look for questions people keep asking and turn them into posts that answer them.

https://t.co/225lnQvkKe

5. Hacker News API

repos.name: shepherd-agents/shepherd
repos.description: A runtime substrate that turns an agent's execution into a reversible, Git-like trace, so meta-agents can observe, fork, replay, and revert any run. Couples agent and environments in a copy-on-write fork ~5x faster than docker commit, with ~95% KV-cache reuse on replay. Framework built for meta-agents to supervise, optimize, and train other agents

tweet.text:
Stanford researchers did it again.

They just built the agent-native version of Git.

When an agent works on a longer task, the run builds up a lot of state.

This includes files edited/created, a dev server, a database, installed packages, KV cache, etc.

Say the agent is at step 10 and makes a mistake, maybe it misreads a traceback and rewrites a file that was actually fine.

The tests start failing, and the run goes off track, although everything through step eight was correct.

By default, the agent just tries to fix it, which creates more edits and tool calls. This burns more tokens and grows the context.

The other options are a person stepping in to redirect it or restarting the whole run from step one.

That's wasteful, because it pays for every model/tool call again and re-prefills the context. Moreover, since an agent's run is non-deterministic, it doesn't reproduce the same early steps anyway.

The reason it's hard to just jump back exactly to a previous correct step and resume from there is that the trajectory is only a message log.

It records what the agent said and which tools it called, but not the live state underneath.

That state includes things like memory, open file handles, child processes, installed packages, /tmp, and KV cache. None of that is in the log.

Git can version the files, but it doesn't snapshot the running process or the KV cache. Checking out step eight moves the files back, but the process is still sitting in step-ten memory with a cold cache.

Shepherd is a runtime layer by Stanford that records the run as a trace of typed events rather than a flat log.

Each agent-environment interaction becomes a commit, similar to Git, but it tracks the live run.

Its commit includes the agent process and the filesystem together, copy-on-write, so a branch carries the actual state and not just the files.

Going back to a previous step is then a single call that forks from that commit and continues from the exact state.

The copy-on-write fork is roughly five times faster than docker commit, and because the prompt prefix through step eight is unchanged, the KV cache is reused over 95% on replay, so early steps aren't reprocessed again.

Once the run can be forked, a meta-agent can sit on top and operate it. It watches the trace and reverts as soon as it looks wrong, before the bad write is committed.

In practice, it's just Python calling fork, replay, and revert on the trace, rather than a separate control plane wired into the harness.

Not everything is reversible though.

Files and sandbox changes undo themselves, but a database write has no automatic undo, so it needs a matching undo step set up in advance.

Something external, like a sent email or a real charge, can't be undone, so the supervisor's job there is to catch it before it fires.

They tested this on a few public benchmarks. On CooperBench, where two agents work on the same codebase, adding a live supervisor took the pair-coding pass rate from 28.8% to 54.7%.

It's still early and labeled alpha. The benefit mostly shows up when a run gets branched a lot over a heavy sandbox state, which is exactly where restarting wastes the most tokens and time.

If Git was made to make file changes reversible, Shepherd is trying to do the same thing for a live agent run.

Shepherd Repo: https://t.co/uUIS57te6g

(don't forget to star it ⭐ )

That said, Shepherd reverts a bad step inside a run. The harness around it, the prompts, tools, and checks the supervisor relies on, still drifts across runs as models and dependencies change.

I wrote about making that harness repair itself, where a failing trace gets diagnosed, the fix is verified against the exact input that failed, and the failure is locked as a regression test so it can't recur. all of this is done using @Cometml's open-source project Opik.

The article is quoted below. https://t.co/YUGDPxpYvy

repos.name: NVIDIA/auto-ontology
repos.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.

tweet.text:
NVIDIA just fixed text-to-SQL’s biggest problem!

the release is called Auto Ontology, and it targets the reason an agent can write valid SQL against a company database and still return the wrong number.

the database stores columns, and the agent has to guess what they mean. a column called extendedprice might hold revenue, and two systems in the same company can define revenue differently.

Auto Ontology gives the agent an ontology, a schema that maps business concepts to the columns that hold them and defines how they relate, before any query is written. it drafts that schema from your database metadata instead of making you write it, and a human certifies it.

the ontology holds three things:

→ terms: business concepts like customer, order, or revenue, with descriptions and synonyms, mapped to the exact columns that store them.

→ SQL attributes: reviewed expressions like a margin or a rolling total, reused so every measure is computed the same way each time.

→ relationships: how tables join, including bridge tables, inferred from keys and the data itself.

to draft these, it profiles columns, samples values, extracts terms table by table, and mines past query history for SQL attributes. everything lands in Postgres, with embeddings in pgvector.

at query time, the agent maps the question to certified terms, follows relationships to find the joins, and writes SQL. it checks filter values against the real data, repairs the query if a check fails, and returns the answer with its SQL and steps.

when the data can't support a question, the agent says so. in NVIDIA's demo, a question about return on ad spend on a sales database with no ad data gets a clarifying reply offering revenue instead of an invented number.

so the ontology tells the agent how to compute an answer and also which questions have one at all.

as the architecture in the image shows, an ingestion service compiles the ontology from your source databases, and any agent harness reaches it through MCP, CLI, or REST API. it supports ten engines including Postgres, Snowflake, Databricks, and DuckDB, runs on Nemotron by default or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and is Apache 2.0.

check it out on GitHub: https://t.co/rHJRxI8LMp

the same principle of defining a schema before the model extracts anything also decides whether agent memory works. I wrote about that in the article quoted below. https://t.co/VW9EyOiy4Z

tweet.text:
GitHub is a freaking GOLDMINE for scraping the internet.

I found 10 insanely powerful repos that can scrape websites, extract millions of data points, and automate your entire research workflow.

And the best part? They're FREE.

Bookmark these:

1. Crawlee for Python

Build powerful crawlers with automatic retries, parallel processing, and browser automation for JavaScript-heavy websites.

https://t.co/6exOpIx1nR

2. Botasaurus

Automate repetitive scraping tasks with browser automation, parallel execution, and caching that saves you from collecting the same data twice.

https://t.co/LeTONNyGdX

3. Jina Reader

Turn messy webpages into clean, AI-friendly text. Perfect for feeding articles, documentation, and research into your AI workflows.

https://t.co/dnoYrImqwB

4. Trafilatura

Extract article text, titles, authors, and publication dates. Export clean research datasets as JSON, Markdown, CSV, and more.

https://t.co/ms8f1vAYQE

5. Spider

Crawl websites concurrently with a Rust-powered engine. Supports JavaScript rendering and runs locally without a cloud account.

https://t.co/2lE6QAfmuQ

6. Crawlab

Manage your crawlers from one dashboard. Schedule jobs, inspect logs, and distribute scraping tasks across multiple machines.

https://t.co/bI56CLB4P4

7. Ferret

Write reusable queries to extract and transform data from websites, APIs, and documents.

https://t.co/Gyu3kSHQOn

8. MechanicalSoup

Automate forms, follow links, and handle cookies with Python. A lightweight option for websites that don’t require JavaScript.

https://t.co/p6lOAYuhqq

9. Selectolax

Extract the exact fields you need from downloaded HTML using a fast parser and CSS selectors. Useful for processing large collections of pages.

https://t.co/QIgnYrVzXP

10. scrapy-playwright

Upgrade your Scrapy projects with browser automation. Render JavaScript, interact with pages, and collect data that ordinary requests miss.

https://t.co/iZPPzBMDlg

The code is free. Hosting, storage, and optional proxies can still cost extra.

I found 10 incredible repos that help you create Hollywood-style animations, motion graphics, animated characters, and stunning visual effects.

And most of them are FREE.

Create full 2D animated productions. Built from Toonz, the software customized and used by Studio Ghibli. Free for commercial and personal projects.

Create vector and raster animations for videos and websites. A dedicated motion graphics app for bringing illustrations, shapes, and designs to life.

https://t.co/lruGQkF8Hd

Capture real movement using two or more ordinary cameras. Turn recordings into 3D motion data for character animation without an expensive motion-capture suit.

https://t.co/L8L4GPTYtT

4. Natron

Combine footage, graphics, and effects through a visual node-based workflow. A free compositor for assembling and polishing visual-effects shots.

https://t.co/QP4AhM42u4

5. Synfig Studio

Animate vector and bitmap artwork without drawing every frame individually. Useful for 2D characters, explainers, and animated scenes.

https://t.co/5T6xgQJotD

6. Effekseer

Create particle effects for spells, explosions, and animated environments. Export effects as 2D animations or integrate them into 3D projects.

https://t.co/tz3HsjWXvt

7. Theatre.js

Choreograph 3D objects, website elements, and interactive scenes. Control animations visually or through code, from subtle interactions to elaborate motion sequences.

https://t.co/FGJvLIQdcl

8. Pencil2D

Make traditional hand-drawn cartoons using bitmap and vector graphics. A straightforward starting point for frame-by-frame character animation.

https://t.co/lajKcMQeL3

9. OpenVDB

Developed by DreamWorks Animation for feature-film volumetric workflows. An advanced library for handling the 3D volume data behind effects, rather than a standalone animation editor.

https://t.co/G3XuBLI7eq

10. SVG.js

Animate vector graphics directly in the browser. Build moving illustrations, animated logos, and interactive diagrams for websites.

https://t.co/2JXr2bfx7U

repos.name: Gaurav-Gosain/tuios
repos.description: A terminal window manager that knows what your agents are doing. Tiling panes, workspaces, sessions that survive restarts, and one Inbox for every coding agent. Official only at tuios.dev and this repo. tuios has no X/Twitter account.

tweet.text:
Half the time, I’m busy trying to figure out which tab has an agent waiting for input.

I’ve got Cloud Code in one pane, Codex in another, and a build process in a third.

And I never know which one needs my attention until I click through every single one.

`tuios` solves this.

It’s a terminal window manager written in Go. Think of it like `tmux`—with tiling and workspaces—but it’s also "aware" of what the agents in your panes are doing: whether they’re actively working, waiting for you, finished with a task, or have encountered an error.

→ Pressing `Prefix+i` opens a unified inbox for the current session—even across different machines.
→ Approvals, questions, errors, and completed tasks all appear in a single list.
→ Respond to prompts directly from that list, without needing to switch to the specific pane.

I was genuinely impressed by `tuios`. It can dispatch the same prompt to multiple agents simultaneously—each running in its own separate Git worktree—and you can even mix and match different "harnesses."

Sessions persist even after a restart. When the daemon comes back online, the inbox lets you resume any ongoing agent interactions.

There is one catch, though: the input model. It’s modal—Vim-style—and pressing `Escape` takes you back to your shell rather than returning you to the window-management mode. If you aren’t a heavy Vim user, there might be a bit of a learning curve.

It’s also packed with features. It might take some time to get the hang of, so be sure to read the documentation carefully.

You can check it out to see if it’s the right fit for your workflow before committing to an installation. Visit https://t.co/UKU8692i4C to run a real app—compiled to WebAssembly—directly in your browser.

It is completely open source.
